title: 5-Year TIPS auction (December reopening, the terminal sale of the October CUSIP) — the one Treasury auction of the year that indirect bidders reliably skip
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), re-fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes — the same byte count the 11-19, 12-23 and 12-24 siblings report, which is the parse's own cross-check), text layer inflated stream-by-stream and re-tokenised into 909 tokens. The row reads verbatim `5-Year TIPS R T / Thursday, December 17, 2026 / Tuesday, December 22, 2026 / Thursday, December 31, 2026`, where Treasury's own legend on that page reads `T --denotes TIPS` and `R --denotes reopening`, making this a REOPENING of the 2026-10-22 new issue tracked as treasury-5y-tips-2026-10-22. The 1:00 p.m. ET competitive close is NOT stated on the schedule; it is inferred here and independently corroborated two ways (53 of 59 5-Year TIPS auctions since 2009 closed 1:00 p.m., and the 12-22 slate puts two bills in the 11:30 a.m. window while leaving the afternoon window uncontested — the 20-Year bond and 2-Year FRN auction 12-23, not 12-22). Stays estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2026-12-17 announcement itself. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md — the id previously existed only as `proposals/treasury-5y-tips-2026-12-22.from-treasury-2y-frn-2026-12-23.json` (2026-09-09), which was read in full first and is now shadowed. Ledger: docs/research/events/treasury-5y-tips-2026-12-22.md. THE LOAD-BEARING FINDING, and it is new to this calendar: the December 5-Year TIPS reopening draws a systematically LOWER indirect share than the June reopening of the same year — 7 of 7 years since the modern cycle began in 2019, mean -13.12 points, t = -3.89 — while bid-to-cover records none of it (-0.07, t = -0.87). Computed from fiscaldata auctions_query (`inflation_index_security: Yes`, 206 records, 59 of them 5-Year, re-pulled this session), percentages on the competitive base (primary dealer + indirect + direct), never total_accepted, because SOMA add-ons ran $0.0-2.6B across the December series. THE CONTROL IS EMPTY ON NOMINALS: over the identical seven Decembers the 5-Year note prints +1.70 (t = 0.78, 3/7 negative), the 7-Year -0.56 (t = -0.13), the 2-Year -6.18 (t = -0.79) and the 10-Year -1.09 (t = -0.55). So it is TIPS-specific, not a December calendar effect. THE ATTRIBUTION FAILS AND IS REPORTED AS FAILED: the October-dated new issue also runs low against the April one (-5.30, t = -1.44, 5/7), and the difference-in-differences that would isolate the December date from the October-dated security is -7.82 with t = -1.41 at n=7 — underpowered, so roughly 40% of the effect may be the security's dating rather than its auction date. THE OBVIOUS MECHANISM IS REFUTED: every December 5-Year TIPS reopening since 2011 settles on the last business day of the calendar year (15/15), which suggests a year-end-turn concession, but the one within-CUSIP test available kills it — in the pre-2019 cycle, where August and December reopened the SAME April CUSIP, December's indirect share ran HIGHER by +6.92 points, 7 of 8, t = +2.85, the opposite sign. STRUCTURE, and it is why pooled base rates on this slot mix two animals: the 5-Year TIPS cycle changed in 2019 from one new issue a year (April, reopened August and December) to two (April and October, each reopened exactly once), so pre-2019 December was the second reopening of an 8-month-seasoned April CUSIP and post-2019 it is the sole reopening of a 2-month-old October CUSIP. In both eras it is the CUSIP's TERMINAL sale, and 2026-12-22 is also the last TIPS auction of 2026 (the schedule's next TIPS row is `10-Year TIPS T`, a new issue, auctioned 2027-01-21). SIZE, stated as a base rate and deliberately NOT re-registered: reopenings print exactly $2B below their own CUSIP's new issue in 31 of 31 scheduled cases since 2011-08 and 15 of 15 on the December leg specifically, so $26B on 2026-10-22 reads $24B here — the informative uncertainty is upstream in the October number, already owned by FT-treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-10-15-1. SESSION MECHANICS: this is a TUESDAY, not the habitual Thursday (13 of 15 prior Decembers), and its when-issued window is 3 business days against the standard 5 — matched only by 2020-12-22, the one other 3-day case. ONE DATED ADJACENT EVENT PROPOSED IN THIS PR: treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-12-17, this event's own confirming primary, previously untracked anywhere while its 12-24 sibling was already carried. Read-it-do-not-trade-it: `symbols: []`, the date is `estimate`, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed.
